channel.title: Money Made Simple
channel.description: Plain-English money guides for students and early-career workers: budgets that stick, first-time investing, credit scores and debt payoff, with the maths shown and no hype.

item.title: The raise you're ignoring: how a 401(k) match works
item.description: A common 401(k) match is 50% of what you contribute, up to 6% of pay. Here's how matches work, how vesting works, and how to check you're getting all of it.

item.title: Acorns review: round-ups are a great habit, but check the fee maths
item.description: Acorns invests your spare change for a flat monthly fee. How the tiers work, why the fee hurts small balances, and who it suits.

item.title: Ally Bank review: the simple online bank with savings buckets
item.description: Ally is an online bank with no minimums, no monthly fees and savings buckets for each goal. What's good and what to watch.

item.title: Are robo-advisers worth it? The fee maths over 30 years
item.description: A robo-adviser's yearly fee looks tiny but compounds. What it costs over decades and the three cases where it's worth paying.

item.title: Aura review: is identity theft protection worth paying for?
item.description: What Aura's credit monitoring, insurance and security tools add, what you can do yourself for free, and who should pay.

item.title: The best bank account for college students: what actually matters
item.description: A student account should be free, never hit you with overdraft fees and help you save. The four checks and options to compare.

item.title: The cheapest ways to file a simple tax return (start with the free ones)
item.description: For a simple return you may pay nothing. VITA, IRS Free File, FreeTaxUSA and TaxAct compared, and how to avoid surprise fees.

item.title: Betterment review: the hands-off way to invest, and what it costs
item.description: Betterment builds and rebalances an index-fund portfolio for you. How its fees work, including on small balances, and when to DIY.

item.title: Budgeting app vs spreadsheet vs notebook: an honest comparison
item.description: The best budgeting tool is the one you'll still open next month. Honest pros and cons of apps, spreadsheets and paper, and how to choose in two minutes.

item.title: CIT Bank Platinum Savings review: great if you have $5,000 saved
item.description: CIT Platinum Savings has paid a top rate on balances of $5,000 or more. Who it suits, what to watch, and picks for smaller balances.

item.title: Debt avalanche vs snowball, with the real maths
item.description: Same three debts, same $200 extra a month. Avalanche saved about $106 in interest; snowball cleared its first debt 12 months sooner. Here's how to pick the method you'll stick with.

item.title: Empower Personal Dashboard review: free net-worth tracking, with a sales pitch attached
item.description: Empower's free dashboard tracks every account and flags investment fees. What it does well and how the paid-advice upsell works.

item.title: The fee that can cost you $18,000: expense ratios explained
item.description: Two funds can own the same stocks and leave you with very different money. How expense ratios work, a 30-year example, and how to check any fund's fee in a minute.

item.title: How to find (and cancel) forgotten subscriptions in 10 minutes
item.description: Search your statements for a handful of words, check your app stores, and use the cancel-or-keep test. A 10-minute audit that usually finds money leaking.

item.title: FreeTaxUSA review: free federal filing that's actually free
item.description: FreeTaxUSA files federal returns free, including freelance income, and charges a small state fee. What's included and what isn't.

item.title: High-yield savings vs money market account vs CD: which one for your savings?
item.description: Three insured places for cash, three trade-offs. What each is, when each wins, and why a money market fund is different.

item.title: How credit scores actually work (and why paying in full can still drop yours)
item.description: The five things that move a FICO score, why your score can dip even when you pay in full, and why closing an old card can hurt. Plain English, no myths.

item.title: How to build a $1,000 emergency fund in 8 weeks
item.description: A starter emergency fund turns a flat tire from a crisis into an errand. Here's an 8-week, $125-a-week plan, where to keep the money, and the rules for using it.

item.title: How to choose a budgeting app: start with what's going wrong
item.description: Name your money problem first, match it to the app built for it, then run a two-week trial that shows whether it's working.

item.title: How to freeze your credit for free (and check your report like an auditor)
item.description: A credit freeze is free by law and makes it much harder for someone to open credit in your name. How to freeze at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, how to thaw it, and 7 things to check on your report.

item.title: How to make a budget you'll actually keep (the weekly-number method)
item.description: Most budgets die in week three. Here's a simple four-line budget built around one weekly spending number, with a worked example and a 20-minute weekly check-in.

item.title: How to move your savings to a high-yield account in 15 minutes
item.description: Step by step: what to check, how to link and transfer, how long it takes, and the setup that keeps your emergency fund growing.

item.title: How to start investing with $100 a month (complete beginner walkthrough)
item.description: What to do before you invest, which account to open, what to buy inside it, how to automate it, and what to do the first time the market drops.

item.title: Is your savings app actually insured? How to check in 5 minutes
item.description: Many savings apps aren't banks. FDIC insurance covers bank failure, not the app company failing. How to find the partner bank, check it in BankFind, and pick a safer account.

item.title: Monarch Money review: the budgeting app for people who want the whole picture
item.description: Monarch tracks every account, budget and goal in one place and works well for couples. Cost, strengths, gaps and alternatives.

item.title: Rocket Money review: is Premium worth paying for?
item.description: What Rocket Money's free version does, what Premium costs, how the bill-negotiation fee works, and when you don't need it.

item.title: Roth or Traditional IRA? It mostly comes down to one question
item.description: Pay the tax now or later? How Roth and Traditional IRAs differ, why many people early in their career lean Roth, what you can withdraw, and how to open one.

item.title: Self credit builder review: how it works, what it costs, and cheaper ways to build credit
item.description: Self builds credit with a small loan saved for you. How it works, its real cost in fees and interest, and cheaper alternatives.

item.title: Sinking funds: how to stop "surprise" expenses wrecking your budget
item.description: Car registration isn't an emergency; it happens every year. Sinking funds turn predictable irregular costs into small monthly amounts. Here's how to set them up.

item.title: SoFi Checking and Savings review: good rate, with one condition to read
item.description: SoFi is a chartered bank with no account fees and a competitive rate, but the top rate has conditions. What to check first.

item.title: Where to open a Roth IRA: a step-by-step for your first one
item.description: Open a Roth IRA in about 20 minutes. How to choose where, the 2026 limit, what to invest in, and the step people skip.

item.title: YNAB review: is You Need a Budget worth $109 a year?
item.description: YNAB has you give every dollar a job. How the method works, what it costs, the trial and student offer, and who should skip it.
